title: Why Fridges Steal 65% of Tomato Flavor 🍅
description:
Why do tomatoes lose their flavor in the fridge? Cold storage turns down the genes that make a tomato's aroma, cutting its smell molecules by up to 65% while the sugar and acid stay the same.

Sources:

topic: Why do tomatoes lose their flavor in the fridge?
script: Your fridge is killing your tomatoes' flavor. Most people never notice why. A ripe tomato's taste isn't just sweet and sour. It's hundreds of tiny smell molecules, and your nose does most of the tasting. Those smells are made by genes inside the fruit, switched on while it sits somewhere warm. But scientists kept tomatoes at five degrees Celsius for a week. The cold turned those genes way down. The smell molecules dropped by up to sixty-five percent! The sugar and acid didn't change at all. So it's still sweet, but it tastes like wet cardboard. Seventy-six taste testers noticed right away. And a week in the cold leaves marks on the fruit's DNA switches, so warming it back up barely helps. Keep ripe ones on the counter instead. So, where are your tomatoes right now?
key_facts: University of Florida researchers (Klee lab, PNAS 2016) stored ripe tomatoes at 5 C for up to 7 days
Flavor volatiles dropped by as much as 65%; sugar and acid did not change
Chilling turned down the activity of genes that make aroma volatiles and changed DNA methylation
A 76-person taste panel rated 7-day chilled tomatoes far less tasty; warming them afterwards barely helped
